title: The $match operators
idea: A `$match` filter is built from query operators: comparisons, lists, logic, existence checks, regex patterns and `$expr` for computed tests.

analogy.text: A shop's filter panel: price above 100, colour in red or blue, in stock. Only products passing every filter stay on screen.
analogy.breaks: The panel offers fixed filters; `$match` accepts any condition, including `$or` and `$expr`.

points: Several conditions in one filter object are combined with AND.
`$or` and `$and` take a list of filters; `$in` takes a list of values.
`$exists` checks that a field is present, not what it contains.
`$expr` runs aggregation expressions, so it can compare two fields or call `$size`.

hero.title: Operators by job
head: Job
Operators
A document passes when
rows: the field compares true to the value
the field equals a listed value ($nin: none of them)
all, any or none of the listed filters pass
the field is present (true) or absent (false)
a string field matches the pattern
hero.caption: Most operators go inside a field: `{ total: { $gt: 100 } }`. `$and`, `$or`, `$nor` and `$expr` go at the top.

code.title: Count what each filter matches
code.caption: Each filter prints how many of the 8 orders it matches. Step through, then press Run.

walk.text: Count what a filter matches. `$count` outputs nothing when no order passes, so return 0.
A comparison on `total` and a list test on `status`.
`$or` takes a list of filters; one match is enough.
`$exists`: no order has a `discount` field, so the count is 0.
`$regex` tests text. `$expr` tests an expression: orders with more than one item.
A real filter: three conditions in one object are ANDed, and `$or` offers two alternatives.

pitfalls: A regex is case-sensitive; add `$options: 'i'` to ignore case.
Repeating a key in a JS object keeps the last; put both operators under one key.
`$exists: true` still matches `null` values; add `$ne: null` to require a value.

quiz.why: Eli matches on city. Ben's 40 and Cleo's 25 pass `$lte: 40`: three orders. `$lt: 40` would skip Ben.

takeaway: Small operators, combined: test each filter by counting what it matches.

starters: When do I need `$expr` instead of a normal filter?
How do I match documents whose array contains a value?
